title: Bohol International Marathon 2026 Review: What the Fourth Edition Was Like
meta_description: Bohol International Marathon 2026 review: a record 5,600+ runners at dawn in Panglao on 30 August, DJs and a sari-sari store on the course, full results.
dek: The Bohol International Marathon's fourth edition drew a record field to Panglao on 30 August 2026. Here is what it was like, from the report on it.
verdict: The Bohol International Marathon is a resort-island marathon that is growing fast. The fourth edition, on 30 August 2026, drew a record 5,600-plus local and international runners onto the roads of Panglao at dawn [1]. It is World Athletics-accredited [1], and the organisers put their effort into looking after runners: airport and seaport welcome lounges, carbo-loading at the start, mobile DJs and stronger hydration stations on the course, and a new sari-sari store refuelling stop [1]. Glady Kiptoo won the marathon in 2:32:40 [1]. The host resort has signed on through 2030 [1]. If you want a destination marathon in the Visayas with a festival feel, this is a strong choice.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition
paragraphs: The 2026 BE Grand Bohol International Marathon, subtitled The Sandugo Run, was held on 30 August 2026 and drew a record crowd of more than 5,600 local and international runners [1]. Runners took to the roads of Panglao at dawn, and the race weekend filled hotels, restaurants and resorts across the island [1].
It was the fourth edition [1]. Organiser Michael Yu said the aim was to support runners from the moment they arrived at the airport to the moment they crossed the finish line [1].

sections.heading: On the Course
paragraphs: The organisers focused on logistics and on-course support [1]. There were welcome lounges at the airport and seaport, carbo-loading preparation at the start, mobile DJs playing along the route, enhanced hydration stations and the race's first sari-sari store stop, offering local snacks as extra fuel for marathoners [1].

Glady Kiptoo won the men's marathon in 2:32:40, ahead of Edsel Moral (2:37:38) and Florendo Lapiz (2:45:34), and Abigael Jerop won the women's in 3:21:40, ahead of April Joy Alampayan [1]. Jhonn Marc Dizon won the men's 21 km in 1:14:32, and Mary Rose Frias the women's in 1:40:33 [1].

sections.heading: A Race With a Long-Term Home
paragraphs: On race day the organisers and host partner BE Grand Resort Bohol signed a renewal that extends the partnership through 2030 [1]. For a young race, a guaranteed home and host for four more years is a good sign of stability.
The organisers say they plan to keep growing the event and attract more international talent [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year?
paragraphs: If you want a marathon holiday on a Philippine island, yes. The race puts real effort into the travelling runner's experience, the field is growing, and a dawn start on Panglao gives you some cool air before the heat.
Book early. The race fills Panglao's hotels on race weekend [1], so reserve a room as soon as you enter.
This review is compiled from a published report on the 2026 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.answer: Glady Kiptoo won the men's marathon in 2:32:40, ahead of Edsel Moral and Florendo Lapiz, and Abigael Jerop won the women's in 3:21:40. Jhonn Marc Dizon and Mary Rose Frias won the 21 km.
